policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'in the tenth year' does not distinguish the qere בַשָּׁנָה from the ketiv בשנת; no mapped textual-variant note decides the unit, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.
ASV explicitly renders the plural 'his eyes shall behold his eyes,' distinguishing the qere plural עֵינָיו from the ketiv singular עינו.
ASV 'walked in thy law' does not distinguish the qere וּבְתוֹרָתְךָ from the ketiv ובתרותך; no mapped textual-variant note decides the unit, so the documented qere base remains the fallback.

ASV 'to cause Judah to sin' does not distinguish the qere הַחֲטִיא from the ketiv החטי, and the mapped note 'Hebrew heart' is a Hebrew gloss rather than a textual variant; the documented qere base therefore remains the fallback.
